recipes.bake: Preheat oven + Dutch oven / stone to 250 C. Bake 20 min lid on (or with steam), then 230 C lid off for 20-25 min until deep brown and 96-98 C inside.
recipes.description: Open-crumb white sourdough with a little wholemeal - the school-average country loaf. About 6 % wetter than a typical home recipe.
recipes.name: Classic sourdough
recipes.notes: Wholemeal ferments faster and drinks more water: if you raise the wholemeal, raise the hydration by ~1 % for every 5 % extra wholemeal.

steps.done_when: Doubled, domed, bubbly, smells yoghurty-sweet. A spoonful floats.
steps.how: Mix ripe starter + flour + water (amounts in the bakesheet). Cover, keep warm.
steps.name: Build levain

steps.done_when: Shaggy dough has hydrated and feels smoother when pulled.
steps.how: Mix the flours with the water EXCEPT ~50 g kept back for the salt. Cover.
steps.name: Autolyse (flour + most of the water)

steps.done_when: Dough holds together and starts to feel elastic.
steps.how: Pinch and fold until fully combined, then slap-and-fold 2-3 min.
steps.name: Mix: add levain, salt, reserved water

steps.done_when: +50-75 % volume, domed edges, bubbles on the sides and top, jiggles.
steps.how: Keep covered and warm (24-26 C). Coil-fold or stretch-and-fold at each alarm.
steps.name: Bulk ferment with folds

steps.done_when: Rounds have relaxed and spread slightly.
steps.how: Tip out, divide (weights in bakesheet), round gently, rest uncovered.

steps.done_when: Surface is taut and smooth.
steps.how: Shape tight boules/batards, seam-up into floured bannetons.
steps.name: Final shape into bannetons

steps.done_when: Slightly risen; a floured finger-poke springs back slowly.
steps.how: Cover bannetons and refrigerate overnight - this is where flavour builds.
steps.name: Cold retard (fridge 3-5 C)

steps.how: Oven to 250 C with Dutch oven or stone inside.
steps.name: Preheat oven + pot/stone

steps.done_when: Deep mahogany crust, hollow knock, 96-98 C in the centre.
steps.how: Straight from the fridge: tip out, score, bake (see bake notes).

steps.how: Cool on a rack. The crumb is still setting - don't cut early.
steps.name: Cool before slicing

recipes.bake: As classic sourdough. Rye browns faster - drop to 220 C for the lid-off stage.
recipes.description: Same averaged base, but 25 % wholegrain (Pain au Levain / Vermont style). Hydration +3 points because bran and rye absorb more water.
recipes.name: Country sourdough (wholemeal + rye)
recipes.notes: The flour blend is a reasoned average of the wholegrain shares in the source formulas, not a copy of any one of them.

recipes.bake: Preheat to 250 C with a stone/steel and a steam tray. Load, add steam, bake at 240 C for 22-25 min. Vent the steam after 10 min.
recipes.description: Classic French baguette on an overnight poolish - average of CIA, Hamelman, SFBI and two Le Cordon Bleu formulas.
flour_blend: Strong white bread flour (or French T65)
recipes.name: Baguette (poolish)

steps.done_when: Bubbly, domed, just starting to dimple/recede in the middle.
steps.how: Flour + water + pinch of yeast (bakesheet). Cover at room temp.
steps.name: Mix poolish

steps.how: Mix remaining flour and water.
steps.name: Autolyse

steps.how: Mix until smooth; moderate gluten development only.
steps.name: Mix: add poolish, yeast, salt

steps.done_when: Nearly doubled, light and airy.
steps.how: Fold gently at each alarm.
steps.name: Bulk ferment with folds

steps.how: Divide, pre-shape into loose cylinders, rest covered.
steps.name: Divide + pre-shape + rest

steps.how: Shape and lay seam-up on a floured couche.
steps.name: Shape baguettes

steps.done_when: Springs back slowly - bake slightly UNDER-proofed for good ears.
steps.how: Covered on the couche.
steps.name: Final proof

steps.done_when: Deep golden, crackling, hollow.
steps.how: 5 overlapping, shallow, nearly-parallel cuts.
steps.name: Score + bake with steam

recipes.bake: Preheat to 230 C (220 C fan). Bake 18-22 min until golden on top AND underneath. Brush with oil as it comes out.
recipes.description: High-hydration olive-oil tray bread - average of the CIA and Bread Ahead formulas (straight dough, no preferment).
extras: Extra virgin olive oil (dough + tray + top)
recipes.name: Focaccia
recipes.notes: For more flavour, refrigerate the dough 8-24 h after the folds (the CIA formula uses a biga for the same reason).

steps.how: Mix flour, water, yeast and salt to a loose, glossy dough.
steps.name: Mix

steps.done_when: Doubled, very bubbly and wobbly.
steps.how: Oil the bowl. Coil-fold at each alarm.

steps.how: Oil the tray generously, ease the dough to the corners.
steps.name: Tray + dimple

steps.done_when: Puffy, bubbles on top, dimples hold.

steps.name: Proof in tray

steps.done_when: Golden top, crisp golden base.
steps.name: Bake

recipes.bake: Egg wash twice. 175 C (160 C fan) for 30-35 min for a tin loaf (12-15 min for small buns) until deep golden and 88-90 C inside.
recipes.description: Rich, egg-and-butter brioche - average of CIA, King Arthur (pro) and Bouchon Bakery formulas. Overnight cold rest for easy shaping.
recipes.name: Brioche loaf

steps.done_when: Silky, pulls from the bowl, passes the windowpane test.
steps.how: Mix everything except butter to full gluten, then add butter a piece at a time.
steps.name: Mix (butter added gradually)

steps.how: Covered, room temperature, then knock back.
steps.name: First rise

steps.done_when: Firm and cold - easy to shape.
steps.how: Flatten on a lined tray, wrap, refrigerate.

steps.how: Divide (weights in bakesheet), roll tight balls, line them up in the tin.
steps.name: Divide + shape into tin

steps.done_when: Domed ~1 cm above the tin rim, springs back slowly.
steps.how: Covered, warm (26-28 C, not hotter or the butter leaks). Egg wash once.
steps.name: Final proof

steps.done_when: 88-90 C in the centre.
steps.name: Second egg wash + bake

recipes.bake: 200 C (180 C fan) for 18-22 min after a second egg wash, until deep golden and the layers at the sides look set.
recipes.description: Laminated yeasted dough - average of CIA, Hamelman and Le Cordon Bleu. Two-day process: dough day, then lamination + bake day.
recipes.name: Croissant / pain au chocolat
recipes.notes: Use high-fat (82 %+) butter for the roll-in. Pain au chocolat: 2 chocolate batons per piece, same dough and timings.

recipes.bake: Cook in plenty of boiling water salted at 10 g per litre: tagliatelle 2-3 min, pappardelle 3-4 min, filled pasta 3-5 min (until they float + 1 min). Save a mug of pasta water for the sauce.
recipes.description: Tagliatelle, pappardelle, lasagne, ravioli, tortellini. The Bologna rule: 100 g flour + 1 egg per person.
recipes.liquid_label: Egg % of flour (whole eggs, out of shell)
recipes.name: Fresh egg pasta
recipes.notes: Richer dough (Emilian style): replace some whole egg with yolks - about 2 yolks for each whole egg removed - and keep the slider about the same. For more bite, swap 20-30 % of the 00 for semola. Freeze nests on a tray, then bag; cook from frozen.

steps.done_when: Smooth and silky, springs back slowly when pressed. Dry? A few drops of water or egg white. Sticky? A little flour.
steps.how: Flour in a mound with a well; eggs in the middle; fork in the flour from the inside, then knead with the heel of your hand ~10 min.
steps.name: Mix (well method) + knead

steps.done_when: Relaxed: it doesn't spring back when you start rolling.
steps.how: Clingfilm, room temperature (or up to a day in the fridge, then 1 h out).

steps.done_when: Tagliatelle: you can see your hand through it. Filled pasta: about 1 mm or less.
steps.how: Machine: widest setting, fold in thirds and re-roll twice, then thinner one notch at a time. Pin: work from the centre outward, turning the sheet.
steps.name: Roll the sheets

steps.done_when: Strands separate cleanly, no sticking.
steps.how: Tagliatelle ~6-7 mm, pappardelle ~2 cm. Dust with semola, form loose nests.
steps.name: Cut / fill + shape

steps.name: Cook + sauce

recipes.bake: Boil in water salted at 10 g per litre: fresh orecchiette or cavatelli 4-6 min, dried ones 8-12 min. Classic: with cime di rapa, garlic, chilli and anchovy.
recipes.description: Egg-free southern Italian dough: re-milled durum semola + lukewarm water, shaped by hand.
recipes.name: Semola pasta (orecchiette, cavatelli)
recipes.notes: Making a lot? Shaping is the slow step: allow about 10-12 min per portion by hand.
